messageCenterItems.title: New Contact Support Experience in Outlook for iOS, Android and Mac
messageCenterItems.summary: A new Contact Support experience is rolling out in Outlook for iOS, Android, and Mac, aligning with the new Outlook for Windows. It uses the existing policy "Allow access to Contact Support in the new Outlook." Rollout starts late November 2026, completing by January 2027. No new policy needed; admins with disabled policies must redeploy.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

We're introducing a new Contact Support experience in Outlook for iOS, Outlook for Android, and Outlook for Mac. This update brings a more consistent way to get help from within the app, aligned with the Contact Support experience available in new Outlook for Windows.

The existing Contact Support policy for new Outlook, "Allow access to Contact Support in the new Outlook" (outlooknew;L_ContactSupport), will also control Contact Support in Outlook for iOS, Outlook for Android, and Outlook for Mac. No new policy is required.

Rollout Schedule:

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

Impact on Your Organization:

The existing Contact Support experience has been replaced with a newer one that improves how users discover solutions for resolving issues on their own. The chat experience provided through Contact Support has not changed, so users can still reach a support agent as they do today. In addition, the Contact Support experience in Outlook for iOS, Outlook for Android and Outlook for Mac now adheres to the same cloud service policy used for New Outlook for Windows.

Action Required/Recommendations:

Contact Support remains available by default when the policy is enabled or not configured, and administrators who disable the policy will remove access to Contact Support in all of these Outlook clients.

IT admins who have already set the existing policy to "Disabled" will need to redeploy their policy once the updated policy becomes available in the Office Cloud Policy Service (OCPS). Redeploying allows the policy to be updated to include the iOS, Android, and Mac endpoints. If the cloud policy is not redeployed, the Contact Support policy will continue to apply only to new Outlook.

No action is required for organizations that have not configured the policy or have it enabled.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Moderation approvals now available across Outlook apps
messageCenterItems.summary: Moderation approvals in Exchange Online will use Actionable Messages adaptive cards across all Outlook clients starting March 2026, completing by November 2026. Dual-mode approvals end July 31, 2026. Moderators must have Microsoft 365 mailboxes. Actionable Messages must be enabled to prepare for this update.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 20, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction

We are updating message Moderation in Exchange Online to streamline how moderators approve or reject messages. These updates improve usability and allow moderators to act from any Outlook client, aligning with customer feedback for simpler, faster approval workflows.

This message is associated with Roadmap ID 492743.

When this will happen:

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Rollout will begin in early March 2026 and complete by end of November 2026 (previously mid-October)

How this affects your organization:

Who is affected:

  • Organizations using message moderation in Exchange Online.
  • Moderators approving messages in Outlook for Windows, Mac, web, and mobile.

What will happen:

  • Moderation approval messages will now use Actionable Messages adaptive cards, allowing inline approve/reject actions in all Outlook clients.
  • Moderators will typically receive a single approval request per moderated message, even when messages are bifurcated or delivered to large distribution lists.
  • Some scenarios may still produce multiple approval messages; each message must be approved for delivery.
  • Dual-mode approvals (legacy voting buttons and new adaptive cards) will be supported until July 31, 2026.
  • After July 31, 2026, only the Actionable Messages adaptive card experience will be supported, and moderators must have their mailbox hosted in Microsoft 365.

What you can do to prepare:

  • Ensure Actionable Messages is enabled (enabled by default). If previously disabled, re-enable using PowerShell:
Set-OrganizationConfig -SmtpActionableMessagesEnabled $true
Set-OrganizationConfig -ConnectorsActionableMessagesEnabled $true
  • Update internal documentation to reflect availability of approvals across all Outlook clients.
  • Notify helpdesk and support staff about the updated approval workflow.

Learn more:

  • Streamlined Moderation Approvals, Now in All Outlook Clients | Microsoft Community Hub
  • Manage message approval in Exchange Online | Microsoft Learn
  • Bifurcation and its technicalities with implications | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.
